transcript: Confession time. I had not actually seen K pop Demon Hunters until very recently. If I'm being honest, I kind of assumed that it just like, would not be the type of movie that I would enjoy. I don't listen to K pop music and I just kind of assumed it was gonna be a fluffy movie about pop stars fighting demons. And having now actually seen the movie, I have to say I was so wrong. It is a movie about pop stars fighting demons, but it is not fluff. There is a tremendous amount of heart and depth to this film, and it actually has something to say. Even the music. Like, these are not just catchy pop songs, although they are certainly catchy, but these are true musical theater songs. They actually had a talk back after the film that was hosted by Benj Pasic and Justin Paul and featured many of the people involved in the creation of the film, from the songwriters to the voice actors to producers. And it really gave me a deeper appreciation for all of the work that went into crafting the story and the songs, how they found that balance between K pop and musical theatre storytelling. Because in the context of the film, these songs are some of the most popular songs in the world. you have to write songs that feel like they could be chart toppers. But then it's also a musical, and so it Has to move the story and the characters forward, and if they don't get both of those things right, the entire movie falls apart. But I think they really nailed that balance, and that's what takes it from being a really good movie to a really great movie. And so if you, like me, have been putting off watching this film, go watch it. Because, one, it's really good, and two, it's nominated for, like, every award, including song of the year at the Grammys, which is just wild for a musical. But, yeah, I was just so pleasantly surprised by this film, and I think you will be, too.
